title: NTSB Issues Preliminary Report on Containership Dali Collision with Francis Scott Key Bridge
text:
The National Transportation Safety Board issued its preliminary report Tuesday on the collision of the cargo vessel Dali with the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore.
The cargo ship experienced two electrical blackouts in port prior to departure and two additional blackouts before striking the bridge support column on March 26.
Six road maintenance workers died in the collapse, and one crew member sustained minor injuries during the incident.
NTSB investigators recovered voyage data recorder audio and electrical system logs from the vessel.

title: Full navigation channel reopens in Baltimore after salvage crews remove Key Bridge wreckage
text:
Federal and state officials announced that the main 700-foot-wide shipping channel into the Port of Baltimore fully reopened Monday following weeks of salvage operations.
Crews removed approximately 50,000 tons of steel and concrete debris from the Patapsco River.
"This milestone restores commercial maritime traffic to one of America's vital ports," Maryland Governor Wes Moore said in a statement.
Commercial cargo vessels began scheduled transit through the channel on Tuesday morning.

title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake strikes eastern Taiwan, triggering tsunami warnings
text:
A powerful magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck off the eastern coast of Taiwan on Wednesday morning, according to the Central Weather Administration.
The earthquake occurred at 07:58 local time at a depth of 34.8 kilometers near Hualien County.
Tsunami advisories were issued for southern Japan and the northern Philippines before being cancelled three hours later.
Emergency authorities reported that at least nine people were killed and more than 900 were injured.

title: Iceland volcano erupts near Grindavík as lava flows toward evacuated town
text:
A volcanic fissure opened on the Reykjanes peninsula in south-west Iceland on Sunday morning, sending molten lava toward the fishing town of Grindavík.
Civil protection authorities completed the emergency evacuation of approximately 3,800 residents before the fissure breached protective earth barriers.
"No lives are in danger, but infrastructure may be threatened," President Guðni Jóhannesson stated on social media.
Flights to and from Keflavík International Airport operated normally throughout the day.

title: The Employment Situation — September 2024
text:
Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 254,000 in September, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1 percent, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.
Employment continued to trend up in food services and drinking places (+69,000), health care (+45,000), and government (+31,000).
Average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose by 13 cents, or 0.4 percent, to $35.36.
Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have increased by 4.0 percent.

title: ECB cuts interest rates again as euro zone growth falters
text:
The European Central Bank lowered its key deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 3.50% on Thursday.
The Governing Council voted unanimously in favor of the reduction following a previous rate cut in June.
"Inflation is expected to rise again in the latter part of this year before declining toward our 2% target next year," ECB President Christine Lagarde told a press conference.
Euro zone headline inflation dropped to 2.2% in August, down from 2.6% in July.

title: Analysis: EU top court cements €2.4 billion antitrust penalty against Google
text:
The European Court of Justice dismissed Google's final appeal Tuesday, upholding a €2.42 billion fine imposed by the European Commission for abusing search market dominance.
The ruling brings a seven-year legal battle over Google Shopping comparison services to a definitive close.
Legal analysts suggest the verdict signals greater regulatory willingness to penalize anti-competitive self-preferencing by dominant platforms.
Google said in a statement that it had modified its shopping product in 2017 to comply with Commission mandates.

title: Sadiq Khan wins historic third term as London Mayor with 43.8% of vote
text:
London Mayor Sadiq Khan secured a third consecutive term Saturday, winning 1,088,214 votes across the capital.
Official election returns showed Khan defeated Conservative challenger Susan Hall by a margin of 276,428 votes, securing 43.8% against Hall's 32.7%.
Voter turnout across Greater London reached 40.5%, slightly lower than the 42.0% recorded in 2021.
"It is the honor of my life to serve the city I love for another four years," Khan said in his victory address at City Hall.

title: Philippines and China trade blame over collision near Second Thomas Shoal
text:
Philippine and Chinese maritime vessels collided near Second Thomas Shoal on Monday during a Philippine resupply mission to stationed troops.
The Philippine military stated that Chinese coast guard vessels deliberately rammed and boarded Philippine naval boats, injuring eight personnel.
China's Coast Guard disputed the account, asserting that the Philippine transport craft illegally intruded into Chinese territorial waters and ignored verbal warnings.
The U.S. State Department condemned what it characterized as dangerous maneuvers by Chinese maritime forces.

title: US East Coast dockworkers launch massive strike as contract negotiations collapse
text:
Around 45,000 members of the International Longshoremen's Association walked off the job at 36 ports from Maine to Texas at midnight on Tuesday.
Union leadership demanded a 61.5% wage increase over six years and strict prohibitions on automated cargo-handling machinery.
The United States Maritime Alliance said in a statement that its latest offer included a wage increase of nearly 50% and protections against full automation.
Supply chain analysts warn that prolonged port closures could cost the U.S. economy up to $5 billion per day.

title: Opinion: The government's cowardly planning reforms will do nothing to solve our housing catastrophe
text:
Ministers have once again shamefully caved in to developer lobbies with a disastrous deregulation bill that will desecrate green belts across England.
The housing secretary announced mandatory local building targets of 370,000 homes a year on Tuesday.
In my view, concreting over the countryside to build unaffordable executive homes is an act of pure vandalism that must be resisted by every community.
We should instead prioritize renovating empty urban properties and taxing land speculation.

title: Tbilisi police clash with thousands protesting controversial 'foreign agents' bill
text:
Georgian security forces deployed water cannon and tear gas to disperse thousands of demonstrators gathered outside parliament in Tbilisi on Tuesday night.
Lawmakers voted 84 to 30 to pass the final reading of the law requiring organizations receiving over 20% of funding from abroad to register as foreign agents.
The interior ministry said 13 police officers were injured and 20 protesters were detained for public order offenses.
Opposition organizers alleged that riot police launched unprovoked baton charges against peaceful crowds.
